text:
Scott Morrow spent the first weeks of the season watching: The Hockey News described a long stretch as a healthy scratch, and he didn't get into a game until Nov. 1. Four games later, The New York Times is asking whether he has "earned lineup spot when New York Rangers regain full health." It's a small sample, but the early answer leans yes. The Rangers have won three straight since a loss in his debut, and they've had 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five.

He's an offensive defenseman and plays like one. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (only seven games, so read it loosely) has him carrying the puck in on 46% of his entries rather than dumping it, and a third of his shots come off the rush.

The case against him is the one that followed him last season. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.14 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, bottom 6% of defensemen, over 454 minutes. He isn't fast by the NHL's skating data, which makes defending the rush harder. We'd watch who sits when the Rangers are healthy.
headline: Scott Morrow is making the Rangers' choice harder
